newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index continued its correction on Friday, but ended off its intraday low in line with the rebound in the domestic A share market after officials denied rumours, brokers said.
The B index closed down 0.505 points or 0.71 percent to 70.439 points after hitting a low of 69.122 points. Turnover was $12 million against Thursday's $18.1 million.
The A share index was up 9.383 points or 0.8 percent to 1,177.849 points after hitting an intraday low of 1142.812 points. Turnover was 8.3 billion yuan, down from 8.8 billion yuan on Thursday.

Widespread rumours saying the exchange would cancel the three-day and seven-day state debt repurchase contracts starting from next Monday were one of the factors depressing shares on the bourse on Friday, brokers said.
The Shanghai stock exchange, asked about the reports, said it is not considering cancelling the contracts.

Brokers said domestic concerns about possible negative news from Beijing during the weekend had been prompted by a series of stories about risk control published in the official Shanghai Securities News.
All 43 B shares traded, with 28 down, eight flat and seven up.
Retailer Shanghai Friendship & Overseas Chinese Co was the biggest loser on liquidation, falling $0.022 or 4.91 percent to $0.426 on volume of 517,300 shares.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co traded the most on institutional liquidation on expectations of unpromising 1996 results, falling $0.016 or 3.21 percent to $0.482 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index reversed the morning losses on institutional support in selective stocks, brokers said.
The SSE 30 index dropped 57.211 points or 1.91 percent to 3,059.843 points.
Wuhan Twin-Tigers Coatings was the star on talk of a plan to offer bonus shares, soaring 0.93 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up of 10.18 yuan on volume of 3.9 million shares.
